resolutions.researcher_notes: No source names a standalone 'Khoms-Melita' pipeline as an operating asset directly, so status is inferred from context per the corridor it purports to be part of, not a literal 'operating' token. Punj Lloyd Group's own 25-years retrospective (Yumpu p.56) confirms the Tripoli-Melita segment was commissioned in March 2010 and gas has flowed from Melita to Zawia Power Plant since, replacing diesel (recurring USD 1bn/yr savings cited) -- clear evidence of an operating gas corridor through this route. OPEC's Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012 Table 4.10 ('Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011') independently lists both 'Khoms/Tripoli' and 'Tripoli/Mellitah' as live Sirte Oil-operated gas lines with length/diameter data for reporting year 2011, confirming operation as of that date. Live opec.org PDF is dead (redirects to homepage, matches the known gotcha); recovered via the 2012-07-22 Wayback snapshot and confirmed with pdftotext (url_verifier FAILs on the raw PDF bytes as expected -- manually confirmed 'Khoms/Tripoli', 'Tripoli/Mellitah', and 'Table 4.10' all present in the extracted text). IMPORTANT CAVEAT carried from the row-level validity review: no source ever names a distinct, standalone 25 km 'Khoms-Melita' object -- every source describes this corridor as the separately-tracked Khoms-Tripoli (~201km) + Tripoli-Mellitah (~158km) segments. These refs support that the Khoms-to-Mellitah gas corridor operates, not that P1789 specifically (as scoped) is a real discrete asset -- flag stands from the rows/P1789.json duplicate assessment.

Both the El Khoms-Tripoli and Tripoli-Melita lines are explicitly named 'Gas Pipeline' projects in Punj Lloyd's own retrospective (Yumpu p.55, 'El Khoms-Tripoli Gas Pipeline' / 'Tripoli-Melita Gas Pipeline'), and OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 lists them under the heading 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (recovered via Wayback + pdftotext, live opec.org link dead per the known ASB gotcha). Two independent, well-corroborated sources for Fuel=Gas. Same corridor-vs-segment caveat as Status applies to whether this specifically supports the 25km 'Khoms-Melita' object.

Punj Lloyd's retrospective (Yumpu p.56) states the government's target for early commissioning of the Tripoli-Melita Pipeline (gas to Zawia Power Plant) was March 2010 and that Punj Lloyd achieved it, with full project completion targeted for 'first half of 2011'. Libya Herald (2020, reporting on a 2020 ICC arbitration ruling) independently corroborates the same timeline, describing the Tripoli-Khoms and Khoms-Mellitah pipeline projects as still under construction when Libya's 2011 revolution halted work. Together these two independent sources support a 2010 construction/commissioning window consistent with ConstructionYear=2010, though again describing the broader corridor rather than a distinct 25km segment.

Punj Lloyd's retrospective (Yumpu p.54) states the Tripoli-Melita Gas Pipeline distributes 'approximately 200 MMSCFD' through the new 34-inch line. 200 MMSCFD converts to ~2.07 bcm/yr (200 x 365 x 0.0283168), a close match to the stated Capacity=2.00 bcm/y (~3% off, consistent with rounding of an approximate figure). This is the only source found with a capacity figure in directly comparable units; OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 does carry a 'Capacity' column for these lines but in units (1,000 scm/yr) that appear to represent cumulative lifetime throughput rather than a nameplate annual rate (values in the tens of millions, i.e. tens of bcm, implausible as an annual rate for a single trunk line) -- did not use it as corroboration because the metric isn't clearly the same thing. Only one strong source found within session search budget (web search was rate-limited/CAPTCHA-walled partway through this shard; DDG, Bing, Ecosia, Mojeek all failed after initial queries) -- tier medium, independent=false pending a second source. Same corridor-vs-segment caveat as other units: this is the Tripoli-Melita segment's nameplate capacity, not confirmed as unique to a standalone 'Khoms-Melita' 25km object.

No source found (English or Arabic) names a distinct 25 km 'Khoms-Melita' pipeline segment. OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 (recovered via Wayback+pdftotext) explicitly lists the two real segments covering this corridor -- 'Khoms/Tripoli' at 125 miles (~201 km) and 'Tripoli/Mellitah' at 98 miles (~158 km) -- neither of which is 25 km. Punj Lloyd's retrospective corroborates similar lengths (150km+7km for El Khoms-Tripoli; a 99km branch plus the broader 1,100km Benghazi-Melita trunk for Tripoli-Melita). No source of any kind puts a 25 km figure on any Khoms-to-Mellitah/Melita gas line. This is consistent with the row-level validity finding (batches/libya-gas/staging/ref-sweep-operating/rows/P1789.json) that P1789 looks like a duplicate/mis-scoped digitization artifact rather than a real distinct 25km asset -- marking UNRESOLVED rather than force-fitting a corridor-level source that doesn't support this specific value.

OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 (Wayback+pdftotext recovery; live opec.org link is dead, known gotcha) lists both 'Khoms/Tripoli' and 'Tripoli/Mellitah' at 34-inch diameter. Punj Lloyd's retrospective (Yumpu p.54) independently confirms 34-inch pipe for both the El Khoms-Tripoli line and the new Tripoli-Melita line. Two independent sources agree exactly on 34in -- the whole Khoms-Mellitah coastal corridor appears to be uniformly 34in trunk line, so this value is well supported at the corridor level even though (per the Length note) the specific 25km 'Khoms-Melita' segment is not independently confirmed to exist as a discrete object.

Libya Herald explicitly names a 'Khoms-Mellitah pipeline project' (tying Khoms and Mellitah together as the two named endpoints), and Punj Lloyd's retrospective (Yumpu p.54) describes gas moving from the Wafa field via Tripoli 'to Melita for processing and distribution' with a compressor station at Melita -- both confirm Khoms and Melita/Mellitah as real, correctly-named endpoint locations on this coastal corridor. StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea=Libya and StartLocation=Khoms/EndLocation=Melita are supported. FLAGGING A CONTRADICTION: EndState/Province is recorded as 'Melita Port', which is not a real Libyan governorate/province -- the Mellitah Complex actually sits in Nuqat al Khams province (as GEM's own P0483/P0484 records correctly show per the row-level validity note). This province field looks like a digitization error and should be corrected/reviewed rather than referenced as-is; the ref supports the place names (Khoms, Melita/Mellitah) only, not the 'Melita Port' province value.

Direct opec.org PDF links are dead (301->homepage); the Wayback snapshot of OPEC ASB 2017 (Table 9.9, 'Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2016') lists 'Jakhira/Intisar (2) | Wintershall | 2 x 50 [mi] | 8, 20 [in]' as a live, tabulated part of Libya's operating gas-pipeline network as of the 2016 data year (confirmed by direct pdftotext extraction of the PDF locally -- the verifier's PDF-binary substring check is a known false negative for this file type, per the script's own documented gotcha). Separately, a live (2024) Sarir Oil Operations tender for firefighting-system upgrades at the 'Jakhira station GOSP' confirms the Jakhira field/station is still an active, maintained facility as recently as 2024 -- consistent with, though not direct literal proof of, this specific gas line still operating today. No source suggests the line has been shut in or decommissioned. [QC] no verified corroborating ref -> unresolved.

OPEC ASB 2012 edition, Table 4.10 ('Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011'), Libya section: 'Jakhira/Intesar | Wintershall | 80 [mi] | 20 [in] | 2,407,250 [1,000 scm/yr] | na'. Capacity column is in thousand standard cubic metres/year, so 2,407,250 x 1,000 scm/yr = 2.40725 bcm/y, matching GEM's recorded 2.40 bcm/y almost exactly (rounding). Confirmed by direct pdftotext extraction of the Wayback-hosted PDF (the live opec.org URL 301-redirects to the OPEC homepage and is dead). No other source located states a throughput/capacity figure for this specific line -- the 2017 ASB edition's equivalent table (9.9) has no Capacity column at all (diameter/length only), and no trade press or company page gives a capacity number for this small interconnector, so this stays single-source/tier=medium despite an extensive search (English + Arabic + alt spellings Jachira/Jakhara/Intisar/Idris/concession 103).

OPEC ASB 2017 edition, Table 9.9 ('Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2016'), Libya section: 'Jakhira/Intisar (2) | Wintershall | 2 x 50 [mi] | 8, 20 [in]'. 2 x 50 miles = 100 miles = 160.9 km, matching GEM's LengthKnown=160.00 km closely (GEM appears to have summed both parallel pipes' lengths, per the source's own '(2)'/'2x' notation). Confirmed via direct pdftotext extraction of the Wayback snapshot (the live opec.org URL is dead, redirects to the homepage). VALUE-CONTRADICTION FLAG: the earlier OPEC ASB 2012 edition (Table 4.10, 2011 data year) shows this as a SINGLE 80-mile/20-inch line (128.7 km), with no second (8-in) pipe and no 160km total -- i.e. the second parallel pipe, and the combined 160km figure, only appear starting with the 2016 data year. Do not cite the 2012 edition for Length (it would show ~129km, not 160km); this is not a data error so much as the pipeline network having been expanded (a second, smaller-diameter line added) between the two data years.

Both OPEC ASB editions (2012 and 2017, Wayback) name the connection 'Jakhira/Intesar' / 'Jakhira/Intisar', matching GEM's Start/EndLocation. Independently (different origin from OPEC), Wintershall Dea's own newsroom confirms Jakhira (Area 91, ex-C96) is a real Sirte Basin field it operated -- via Wintershall Aktiengesellschaft (WIAG) -- until operatorship transferred to Sarir Oil Operations (a WIAG/NOC joint venture) on 29 October 2020; a separately located, independent pumpsandsystems.com trade article (2015) also describes 'a gas processing plant at the Jakhira site' in the Sirte Basin desert, further corroborating the start point. Intesar/Intisar is a separate, large, well-documented Sirte Basin field (Occidental discovery, 1967; part of the Zueitina Oil Co. concession per USGS Minerals Yearbook 2016, distinct from Wintershall's own concession) -- corroborated across OPEC ASB, USGS, and Wood Mackenzie field reports, all independent of GEM. CAVEAT: StartState/Province and EndState/Province are both recorded as 'Sirte Basin', a geological/informal region rather than a Libyan administrative province (Jakhira sits in the Al Wahat district per Wintershall Dea's own description) -- a minor precision issue, not a contradiction, and consistent with how sibling rows in this batch are recorded.

This batch's KNOWN GOTCHA applies: the live opec.org ASB2012 link (per seed_citations) is dead (redirects to homepage; url_verifier returns 200-but-missing-token because the PDF's text stream is compressed and the naive substring check can't reach it). Recovered via Wayback (https://web.archive.org/web/20120722013100/.../ASB2012.pdf, CDX-confirmed live capture) and manually ran `pdftotext -layout` -> Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011', Libya section, p.75, exact row: 'Bouri/Bahr Assalam | Mellitah Oil and Gas | 20 [mi] | 10 [in] | 3,879,921 [1,000 scm/yr] | na'. This is a specific named match for this exact pipeline, listed as extant transport infrastructure in 2011 (not proposed/planned) -- supports Status=operating. Second, independently-recovered OPEC snapshot (ASB2017, Wayback https://web.archive.org/web/20231204014748/.../ASB2017_13062017.pdf, manually pdftotext'd, Table 9.9 'Main gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2016', p.133-134) still lists 'Bouri offshore/Bahr Es Salam (2) | Mellitha Oil & Gas | 2 x 12 [mi] | 4, 10 [in]' -- confirms the route was still active 5 years later (2016 data), now apparently with a second parallel line added (4in) alongside the original 10in line. Third, independent (non-OPEC) source: Mellitah's own corporate 'About the Company' page (mellitahog.ly, Arabic, verified live) states Mellitah Oil & Gas operates both the Bouri field (130km north of Tripoli) and the Bahr Essalam field (110km northwest of Tripoli), i.e. confirms the company is currently, actively running both endpoints of this corridor. Three origins (OPEC statistical body across two editions, and Mellitah's own site) -- tier high. Note: ASB2017's length figure for the 10in line (12 mi) differs from ASB2012's (20 mi) for the same route -- see Length unit notes for this discrepancy; it does not affect the Status determination.

Fuel=Gas is definitional to the recovered OPEC ASB2012 table this row sits in ('Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011', Table 4.10, p.75 -- as opposed to Table 4.11, the parallel petroleum-products-pipeline table a few pages later, which lists a different Libya roster) -- see Status notes for the Wayback recovery/pdftotext method. Independent corroboration: the Wikipedia 'Greenstream' pipeline article (verified live, contains both 'Bouri' and 'Bahr Essalam') states the Bahr Essalam offshore field, Bouri Field, and Wafa field all feed gas into the Mellitah complex/compressor station that supplies the Greenstream export line to Sicily -- consistent with a gas (not oil) pipeline linking Bouri to Bahr Essalam/Mellitah. Two independent origins (OPEC statistical body vs. a general encyclopedia entry on the export pipeline this corridor feeds) -- tier medium given neither source is pipeline-specific/dedicated on fuel type alone.

CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: Recovered Wayback ASB2012, Table 4.10, Libya, 'Bouri/Bahr Assalam' row gives Length = 20 miles = 32.19 km (20 x 1.609344), which is a close match to the sheet's LengthKnown value of 32.00 km (~0.6% / ~0.2km apart) -- clearly the same table row given the exact-match Diameter (10in) and Capacity (3,879,921) also line up (see those units), so I'm confident this is GEM's original source. However, the later OPEC ASB2017 recapture of the same route (Table 9.9, 2016 data, manually pdftotext'd) gives a materially different figure: 'Bouri offshore/Bahr Es Salam (2) | Mellitha Oil & Gas | 2 x 12 [mi] | 4, 10 [in]' -- i.e. by 2016 OPEC records TWO parallel lines of 12 miles (19.3km) each, diameters 4in and 10in, rather than one 20-mile 10in line. This could mean: (a) a second, smaller-diameter line was added between 2011 and 2016 alongside the original, and/or (b) the route was re-surveyed/re-measured (12mi vs 20mi is a large, non-trivial change, not a rounding artifact). Since the sheet's row is specifically the 10in line (matching Diameter exactly) and its length (32.00km) tracks the 2012 figure far better than the 2016 one, I'm citing ASB2012 as the primary support and flagging the ASB2017 discrepancy rather than citing it as corroboration (it would actually contradict, not confirm, the sheet's length value) or fabricating an explanation. tier low given this unresolved cross-edition conflict on length specifically (Diameter and Capacity are not affected by it).

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: Greenstream is a real, extensively documented subsea international gas transmission pipeline (not a hallucination, not a gathering/feeder line) linking Libya's Mellitah gas complex to Gela, Sicily, Italy — operated by Eni/NOC Libya since 2004. Confirmed via Wikipedia, Reuters (2011 and 2013, both via Wayback since live Reuters 401-bot-walls this UA), Wood Mackenzie, Oil & Gas Journal, and a Weatherford/PPSA engineering case study — five independent origins, all naming the pipeline explicitly (the sheet's own cited sources are not GEM-derived filler). ROUTE/LOCATION: Mellitah Complex, Libya -> Gela, Italy confirmed identically across all 5 sources. OWNER: Eni SpA + Libyan National Oil Corp confirmed (OGJ: 'Libya's National Oil Company and Eni SPA each held equal shares in Greenstream BV Libyan Branch'; Wikipedia: Agip Gas BV JV of Eni and NOC) — matches GEM's Owner1/Owner2 exactly. STATUS='operating' confirmed across a 2011-2013 span despite a Feb-Oct 2011 civil-war shutdown (Reuters 2011 test-restart article, Reuters 2013 Berber-blockade article) — intermittent disruption does not change base classification. DUPLICATE CHECK: no other pipeline in the 30-row Libya roster runs to Italy/Gela or is subsea; not a duplicate of P0483 (Libya Coastal, Mellitah->Benghazi, domestic) or any other row. SEGMENTCOST: GEM's $6,600,000,000 matches the Arabic RT article's '$6.6 billion' construction-cost figure exactly. LENGTH: GEM's 520.00 km is the majority reading — Reuters 2011 (via Wayback) states 'The 520 km Greenstream pipeline...' verbatim and Wood Mackenzie states 'total length of the pipeline is 520 kilometres' — two independent sources matching GEM exactly. Minor caveat: Wikipedia and an Arabic RT (rt.com) article both instead give 540 km, and the Weatherford/PPSA case study gives 322 miles/518km — so there is a genuine 518-540km spread in the literature, but 520km (GEM's value) is directly supported by 2 independent sources verbatim, so treat as confirmed with this spread noted rather than a material conflict. DIAMETER: GEM records a composite '36, 32, 10' in — the subsea trunk's 32in diameter is independently confirmed twice (Wikipedia: 32in/810mm; PPSA case study: '32 inch diameter'); the additional 36in and 10in figures (likely onshore compressor/delivery segments) are plausible for a multi-segment GEM record but were not independently verifiable from the sources found — not contradicted, just unconfirmed.

resolutions.recommendation: correct Capacity — GEM's 20.00 MMcf/d is off by roughly 40-50x versus every independent source; real-world nameplate is ~8-11 bcm/year (~774-1,064 MMcf/d)
resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM records Capacity=20.00 MMcf/d. This materially disagrees with every independent source found: Reuters 2011 (via Wayback, verbatim) states 'has a capacity of 8 billion cubic metres'; Wikipedia states initial capacity 8 bcm/year later increased to 11 bcm; the Arabic RT article independently states 'capacity reaches over 8 billion cubic meters annually.' Converting: 8 bcm/year = 35.3147 bcf/year = ~773.9 MMcf/day; 11 bcm/year = ~1,064 MMcf/day. So the real nameplate capacity is roughly 774-1,064 MMcf/d, not 20 MMcf/d — a ~40-50x discrepancy, almost certainly a unit-conversion or data-entry error (e.g. a bcm figure mis-mapped into an MMcf/d field, or a decimal/order-of-magnitude slip). This is corroborated by 3 independent sources (Reuters, Wikipedia, RT-Arabic) all agreeing with each other and all disagreeing with GEM, so flagging per the 'material disagreement' rule rather than silently passing it. Not proposing a specific replacement number as a hard fix (units need reconciling by whoever maintains the sheet's Capacity/CapacityUnits convention), but the correct order of magnitude is clearly ~800-1,000+ MMcf/d, not 20.

resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM's own gem.wiki page for this pipeline carries exactly one citation: 'World Energy Atlas, Petroleum Economist, 2001' — a print atlas with no URL, unverifiable and (per standing rules) not citable regardless. wiki_citations.json independently confirms zero harvestable citations for this row. So the sheet has never had an independently checkable source for this entity at all. I then tried to independently confirm the pipeline via the SAME authoritative source that underpins nearly every other pipeline in this 30-row Libya gas roster: OPEC's Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012, Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (p.75; live opec.org copy 301-redirects to the homepage, retrieved instead via the Wayback Machine capture and confirmed with curl+pdftotext, since url_verifier's substring screen cannot read binary PDF byte streams — same documented false-negative as sibling row P1869). That single OPEC table lists 21 named Libyan gas pipelines and its length/diameter/capacity figures match — essentially exactly, after mi->km and 1,000 scm/yr->bcm/y conversion — 21 of the ~30 pipelines on this project's in-scope roster: Wafa/Mellitah=P0484, Bahr Assalam/Mellitah=P1855/P6713, Mellitah/Gela=P0439 (Greenstream), Intesar/Brega=P1856 (207mi=333km, 42in, 42,480,884 th.scm/yr=42.48 bcm/y — exact match to P1856's cap=42.48), 103D/103A=P1857, Bu-Attifel/Intesar=P1858/P6714, Bouri/Bahr Assalam=P1859/P6709, Waha/Nasser=P1860, Faregh/Intesar=P1861, Brega/Benghazi=P1862, Brega/Khoms=P1863, Khoms/Tripoli=P1864, Tripoli/Mellitah=P1865, Nasser/Brega=P1866, Attahaddy/km-91.5=P1867, Km-81.5/Brega=P1868, Raguba/km-110=P1869, Intesar/Sahel=P1870, Sahel/km-81.5=P1871, Km-91.5/Brega=P1872, Jakhira/Intesar=P1873. This is clearly the (or a) primary data backbone GEM drew this roster from. Crucially, THERE IS NO 'Defa' ENTRY ANYWHERE IN THIS TABLE — not under any of the Libya rows in Table 4.10 (gas), and I also checked Table 4.9 'Crude oil pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (pp.71-72) in the same document in case Defa's line was misclassified as oil — it is also absent there (that table's Libya section lists Sarir/Tobruk, Messla/Amal, Nasser/Al-Brayqah, Amal/Ras Lanuf, Aseida/Ras Lanuf, etc., but no Defa route of any kind). P0482 is one of only a handful of roster rows (alongside P0483 Libya Coastal [a rollup, expected], P3987, P3988, P6705, P1789) missing from this table, and it is distinctive in that its Diameter and Capacity are BOTH still blank in the mainsheet — unlike every OPEC-sourced row, which has all three of length/diameter/capacity populated from that table. Separately, I confirmed 'Defa' IS a real place-name in Libya's Sirte Basin: two Wikipedia geology articles ('Zelten oil field' and 'Raguba field'), both citing a USGS Sirte Basin Province assessment and an academic paper (Belazi, 'The geology of the Nafoora oil field, Sirte basin, Libya', Journal of Petroleum Geology v.12, 1989), describe Defa as one of the Sirte Basin's 'giant oil fields' in the north-center trend, sometimes styled jointly as 'Defa-Waha field' — so the field itself is not invented. But no source found ties Defa to Brega by a dedicated 299km gas line. The only named 'Defa' pipeline I could find anywhere is on Wikipedia's 'Ras Lanuf' article, which twice describes a 'Defa-Ra's Lanuf' OIL pipeline (~251km) — a different commodity and a different endpoint than GEM records — but that specific claim's own citation is Theodora.com/pipelines, a source this project blocklists as an unreliable tertiary aggregator, and it is NOT corroborated by the OPEC table either, so I cannot treat it as confirmation of anything, only as a hint that if a real 'Defa' pipeline exists in the literature at all, everything else about it (commodity, endpoint) contradicts GEM's P0482 record. Net: I could not independently confirm P0482 as a real, distinct, operating 299km Defa-to-Brega GAS pipeline from any source — GEM's own citation is unverifiable, the authoritative OPEC dataset that backstops almost this entire roster is silent on it (in both its gas AND oil tables), and the one 'Defa' pipeline name that does surface in the wider literature points to a different route and commodity, sourced from a source this project excludes. This meets the sweep's 'GEM-only entity' flag criteria.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: confirmed real and correctly classified. The sheet's own two citations: (1) a Facebook photo link — 200 live but no extractable text, useless as a spec source (not cited); (2) a World Bank/Tractebel Engineering report 'Fuel Availability & Opportunities for Cost Reduction Report' (Libya: Supporting Electricity Sector Reform, 18 Dec 2017) — verified live (200) via WebFetch + manual pdftotext extraction (url_verifier's automated substring screen false-negatived on this PDF per its own documented PDF-extraction caveat; I confirmed the exact phrases manually). This report independently and repeatedly describes a '34" Coastal Pipeline system with a total longitude of ~1,120 km' connecting Libya's West and East gas network areas via Mellitah (West Entry Point) -> Marsa El Brega -> Benghazi (East Entry Point) — matching GEM's recorded endpoints (Mellitah Complex->Benghazi), diameter (34in, exact match) and length (1164km vs source's ~1120km, ~4% high, within normal rounding tolerance). Status=operating and Fuel=Gas are both well-supported by extensive context (flows, injection, consumption figures) even though the literal word 'operating' isn't required per the confidence-tier rules. Owner1='Libyan National Oil Corp' 100% is plausible: the source states NOC 'is in charge of exploration, production, transportation and commercialization of O&G' and that a NOC subsidiary, General Gas Transmission and Distribution Company (GGT&D, est. 2007), specifically 'construct[s] and manage[s]' the gas distribution/transmission network — so GGT&D may be the more precise operator/owner-of-record than the parent NOC, but NOC as ultimate state owner is not wrong. DUPLICATE CONCERN: the same World Bank source explicitly decomposes this 'Coastal Pipeline' into constituent legs that GEM ALSO tracks as separate ProjectIDs on the in-scope roster: the western leg (871km total) splits into a Mellitah->Tripoli->Khoms trench (222km, ~600 mmscf/d nominal) and a Brega->Khoms trench (645km, ~370 mmscf/d) — the latter length matches P1863 'Brega-Khoms Gas Pipeline' (645km) almost exactly; and the eastern leg is Marsa El Brega->Benghazi (246km, ~410 mmscf/d), the same route as P1862 'Brega-Benghazi Gas Pipeline' (though P1862's recorded length of 396km diverges from the source's 246km for that same leg — a separate P1862 issue, out of scope here but worth flagging to whoever re-audits P1862). P1865 'Tripoli-Mellitah' (158km) and P1864 'Khoms-Tripoli' (201km) together (359km) roughly correspond to the source's single 222km Mellitah-Tripoli-Khoms trench, again not a clean 1:1 match but clearly the same physical corridor split differently. Net effect: GEM appears to carry BOTH a system/network-level 'Coastal Pipeline' entity (P0483, cluster/rollup framing, len 1164/cap 604) AND its physical constituent segments as separate full-attribute rows (P1865/P1864/P1863/P1862) — this is the exact 'dual-level granularity' pattern this project's own reconciliation SOP acknowledges (network-grouping rows vs individual segment rows) and it risks double-counting length/capacity if both are summed in aggregate tracker statistics. This is a structural/dedup issue, not a fabrication — recommend NOT silently deleting either level, but flagging for a maintainer decision on which layer carries the aggregate totals.

resolutions.recommendation: Leave Capacity sourced but flag as approximate/unconfirmed — no independent source gives a single 604 MMcf/d end-to-end figure; also flag StartYear1=1983 as unconfirmed.
resolutions.researcher_notes: GEM records a single Capacity=604.00 MMcf/d for the whole Mellitah->Benghazi corridor. The one strong independent source I could verify (World Bank/Tractebel 2017 report, same doc used above) gives THREE DIFFERENT segment-level nominal capacities for this same corridor rather than one system-wide number: ~600 mmscf/d (Mellitah->Tripoli->Khoms trench), ~370 mmscf/d (Brega->Khoms trench), and ~410 mmscf/d (Brega->Benghazi eastern leg). None of these equals 604, and a true through-line bottleneck capacity for a corridor built from unequal segments would logically be capped near the lowest segment (~370 mmscf/d), not 604 — so 604 looks like it may conflate/round the western Mellitah-Khoms trench figure (~600) rather than represent genuine end-to-end throughput. This is a material disagreement per the sweep's own rule ('mentions the pipeline' is not enough — the source must agree with the GEM number), so I'm not passing Capacity as confirmed. Separately, the sheet's StartYear1=1983: I found no source (this report or otherwise) corroborating a 1983 construction/inauguration date for this pipeline specifically — the report's only nearby '1983' reference is the unrelated Tobruk power STATION commissioning date, which is plausibly where a wrong 1983 could have been transcribed from if that ever happened, though I have no direct evidence of that mix-up, only that 1983 is unconfirmed as-is. Recommend Baird's team keep both fields but treat them as unverified rather than sourced.

resolutions.recommendation: Do not treat 13.00 bcm/y as confirmed. It most likely originated from conflating the operator's daily delivery figure (13 MMSm3/day through the 32in line) with an annual bcm figure -- 13 MMSm3/day annualizes to roughly 4.7-4.9 bcm/y, not 13 bcm/y. No independent source states a 13 bcm/y annual capacity for this specific pipeline. Either correct to the ~4.7-4.9 bcm/y actual-throughput figure (with a note that it's delivery, not nameplate capacity), or leave Capacity blank pending a source with an explicit annual bcm figure for this pipeline specifically (as opposed to the broader Mellitah complex/Greenstream export capacity of 8-11 bcm/y).
resolutions.researcher_notes: Capacity field was MISSING_REF (no existing citation) with value 13.00 bcm/y. Sources found: mellitahog.ly's gas-division/production page states 'the average gas delivery is about 13 MMSm3/day' through the 32in Wafa-Mellitah pipeline (this is a daily figure, not annual -- annualized it is ~4.7-4.9 bcm/y, not 13); pipeline-journal.net states the downstream Greenstream export pipeline has 'an annual capacity of 8 billion cubic meters (bcm)'; other reporting places the Mellitah complex's overall design capacity at 10.0 bcm/y (8 bcm/y exported via Greenstream + 2 bcm/y to the domestic market). None of these support a 13 bcm/y figure for the Wafa-Mellitah gas pipeline itself -- the '13' in GEM's Capacity field looks like a units mix-up with the operator's '13 MMSm3/day' delivery statistic. Left as a flagged concern rather than a confident fill since I could not independently verify any single authoritative annual-bcm figure specific to this pipeline segment.

(2) sirteoil.com.ly/?p=8754 -> the live site has been rebuilt as a JS SPA that serves only a blank shell for this old query-string URL (confirmed 200 but empty content, no article); the Wayback snapshot (archive timestamp 2021-06-19, verified live and containing the expected Arabic terms) recovers the original article, which is a tour report by Sirte Oil Co's board chairman of western-region gas facilities. Crucially, that source does NOT describe a 'Khoms-Melita' pipeline as a discrete object -- it explicitly names the route as two separate lines, quote: "خط 'الخمس - طرابلس' 'طرابلس - مليتة' تم تشغيله مبكراً..." (the 'Khoms-Tripoli' / 'Tripoli-Mellitah' line was commissioned early...), i.e. the exact same segment names GEM already tracks separately as P1864 (Khoms-Tripoli, 201 km) and P1865 (Tripoli-Mellitah, 158 km). The article does use an informal umbrella phrase 'الخط الطولي الخمس مليته' (the Khoms-Mellitah longitudinal line) for job titles/administrative purposes (e.g. 'منسق العمليات والخط الطولي الخمس مليته'), confirming Sirte Oil Co. operates this corridor as a unit -- which supports Operator=Sirte Oil Co as plausible -- but gives no support for a physically distinct 25 km segment called 'Khoms-Melita'. Geographically, Khoms and the Mellitah Complex are roughly 220 km apart by straight line (and ~360 km by the P1864+P1865 route length, consistent with a coastal detour through Tripoli); a 25 km pipeline cannot span that distance, so this cannot be read as a shorthand/simplified version of the same route. I could find zero independent sources (web search in English and Arabic) that describe a distinct 'Khoms-Melita'/'Khoms-Mellitah' pipeline with a 25 km length, 34-inch diameter, or 2 bcm/y capacity -- every hit either is GEM's own wiki page or is unrelated. GEM's own separately-cited Libya Coastal Gas Pipeline page (read for structural context only, not cited here) describes the same Khoms-to-Mellitah stretch as the 'western segment' of that single 1164 km trunk (nominal 600 mmcf/day), reinforcing that this corridor is already modeled elsewhere in the dataset (P0483 in aggregate; P1864+P1865 at segment level) and that P1789's very short 25 km / 2 bcm/y figures do not correspond to any documented physical asset. Net: existence of *a* Khoms-Mellitah gas corridor is real, but the specific object recorded under P1789 (a standalone 25 km, 34in, 2 bcm/y line) looks like a duplicate/fragment -- most plausibly a mis-scoped or badly digitized artifact from the (now-dead) Harvard worldmap dataset -- rather than a distinct physical pipeline. Location field is also internally inconsistent: EndState/Province is populated with 'Melita Port', which is not a real Libyan province (the real province for Mellitah is Nuqat al Khams, as recorded correctly on P0483/P0484), another sign this row was carelessly assembled.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The Zueitina source states the project's gas delivery targets in mmcf/day, not bcm/y: Phase 1 = ~250 million standard cubic feet/day; full build-out (all phases) = ~1500 million standard cubic feet/day. Converting for cross-check: 1500 mmcf/d x 28,316.85 m3/mmcf = ~42.475 million m3/day (Mm3/d) -- this is suspiciously exactly GEM's recorded Capacity figure of 42.48. That strongly suggests GEM's Capacity value was taken directly from this project's daily mmcf/d target, correctly converted to million m3/DAY, but then mislabeled with CapacityUnits='bcm/y' (billion m3/YEAR) instead of the correct daily unit. Annualizing correctly: 42.475 Mm3/d x 365 = ~15.5 bcm/y -- so even at the FULL eventual build-out target, capacity should read ~15.5 bcm/y, not 42.48 bcm/y (a ~2.7x overstatement as currently recorded); and Phase 1 alone (250 mmcf/d) is only ~2.6 bcm/y. This is a clear, quantifiable spec error, not just a rounding disagreement. I'm not proposing a specific corrected number as a confident fill because it's unclear whether the pipeline today (2026) has reached the full 1500 mmcf/d build-out or remains at an intermediate phase -- flagging for correction/verification rather than guessing.

Even setting the dead-link problem aside, the OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin is a country-level aggregate reserves/production/trade tables publication — it has never itemized named internal Libyan gas-gathering pipeline segments like 'Waha-Nasser', so it would not have supported this specific claim even when live. Checked wiki_citations.json for the other 29 in-scope rows: this EXACT same ASB2012.pdf URL is reused verbatim as the sole citation on at least 10 sibling pages (P1859, P1861, P1866, P1867, P1868, P1869, P1870, P1871, P1872, and P1860 itself) — confirming it is a boilerplate/generic citation pasted across a whole cluster of Sirte Basin internal segment pipelines, not evidence specific to any one of them. Open-web search (English and Arabic) for 'Waha-Nasser gas pipeline' returns only gem.wiki itself and its mirrors/aggregators; nothing independent names a pipeline called 'Waha-Nasser'. Independently confirmed both endpoints are real, distinct entities: Waha field is operated by Waha Oil Co (NOC/ConocoPhillips/TotalEnergies/Hess JV), while Nasser field (formerly Zelten, Libya's first major oil field, discovered 1959) is ~169 km south of Brega and is operated by Sirte Oil Co, a DIFFERENT NOC subsidiary (offshore-technology.com field profile, Wikipedia Zelten oil field, globalsecurity.org Libya petrol background) -- i.e. current Operator/Owner values (Waha Oil Co / NOC+ConocoPhillips+TotalEnergies+Hess) describe the Waha-side JV only and may not be the right attribution if this pipeline genuinely runs to Nasser field's Sirte-Oil-operated infrastructure. One WebSearch AI-summary claimed globalsecurity.org lists 'Defa-Nasser; Nasser-Hatiba; Nasser(Zelten)-Marsa el Brega; Waha-Es Sider' as Libya's major pipelines (notably NOT 'Waha-Nasser') — but I fetched that page directly and this pipeline list does NOT appear anywhere in the actual HTML; the search tool's synthesis appears to have fabricated/merged it from elsewhere, so I am explicitly NOT relying on or citing it. Net: no independent source of any kind could be found that names a 'Waha-Nasser' gas pipeline, the row's own cited source is both dead and generically non-specific (and is reused wholesale across ~10 other rows), and there is a plausible mechanism for how it could be a conflation (two real, separately-operated Sirte Basin fields/nodes stitched into a pipeline name GEM invented for a network diagram). Recommend treating as an unconfirmed/possible-hallucination entity pending a real primary source (Waha Oil Co / NOC technical document, EIA/USGS Sirte Basin infrastructure map, or a news report) rather than accepting the current spec values (177 km / 24 in / 5.66 bcm/y / operating) at face value. Did not add any refs — nothing passed verification.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The gem.wiki page's sole citation is 'Annual Statistics Bulletin, OPEC, 2012, p.75' -> https://www.opec.org/opec_web/static_files_project/media/downloads/publications/ASB2012.pdf. On its face this is exactly the 'generic citation that doesn't name the pipeline' existence trap the brief warns about, and a sibling shard in this same batch (P1860, Waha-Nasser) reached an existence-concern verdict for the identical reason — it stopped at the dead live link and concluded the ASB could never have itemized named internal segments even when live. I do NOT think that conclusion holds: I pulled the SAME 2012 document from the Wayback Machine (http://web.archive.org/web/20250110032615/https://opec.org/opec_web/static_files_project/media/downloads/publications/ASB2012.pdf, confirmed a genuine 7.8MB PDF via `file` + pdftotext, not an HTML shell) and it turns out Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (p.75) DOES itemize named Libyan segment-level pipelines row by row. The exact row: 'Faregh/Intesar   Waha   110   24   7,080,147   na' under columns Length(miles)/Diameter(inches)/Capacity(1,000 scm/yr). Converting: 110 mi = 177.0 km (GEM LengthKnown=177.00, exact match), Diameter 24 in (GEM=24.00, exact), Capacity 7,080,147 thousand scm/yr = 7.080 bcm/yr (GEM=7.08, exact), Owner/operator 'Waha' (GEM Operator='Waha Oil Co', matches). This is not a coincidental match — the same archived table also contains rows that line up 1:1 with several sibling roster pipelines (e.g. 'Waha/Nasser' 110mi/24in/5,664,118 -> P1860's 177km/24in/5.66bcm; 'Intesar/Brega' 207mi/42in/42,480,884 -> P1856's cap 42.48), confirming this whole 30-pipeline Libya-gas cluster in the GEM sheet was seeded from this exact 2011 OPEC statistical table. So: existence and every recorded spec (Status=operating [inferred from table's presence in an active-infrastructure statistics table], Fuel=Gas, Capacity, Length, Diameter, Operator) are CONFIRMED against a genuine, independent, official industry-statistics source — url_verifier's automated FAIL on the Wayback link is a content false-negative (raw-byte substring check can't read PDF-internal text streams; the doc's own docstring flags this class of miss), and I resolved it manually via `pdftotext -layout` extraction rather than discarding the source. Caveats keeping this at 'confirmed (caveat)' rather than a clean pass: (1) this is a single source (OPEC 2011/2012 bulletin) — no second, fully independent source was found in extensive EN-language web search (all hits are gem.wiki itself, its mirrors, or a DIFFERENT, newer, unrelated pipeline — see below) — so tier is medium, not high; (2) the OPEC figure is an ~2011 snapshot; nothing found independently reconfirms this specific 24-in Faregh-Intesar segment is still flowing in 2026, though the Faregh field itself is confirmed very much active (Waha Oil brought two new gas wells online there per 2026 reporting) and there is no evidence of this line's retirement, so 'operating' remains the reasonable read. DUPLICATE CHECK: web search surfaced a completely different, much newer pipeline that is easy to confuse with this one by name — the 'Farigh-Brega' / 'Intisar A/103-Brega' gas pipeline that Libya's NOC just tested in April 2026 after a 16-year stall (42-inch, ~130 km, connecting Intisar A/103 gas field to the Brega distribution network, commissioned by Sirte Oil Co and Zueitina Oil Co, not Waha) per Ecofin Agency, energycapitalpower.com and Pipeline Technology Journal reporting. Diameter (42 in vs 24 in), length (130 km vs 177 km) and operator (Sirte/Zueitina vs Waha) all differ, so this is NOT the same physical line as P1861 and not a duplicate — but flagging it explicitly since the names are confusingly close and a future sweep could easily conflate them.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The gem.wiki page's ONLY cited source is 'Annual Statistics Bulletin, OPEC, 2012, p.75' (opec.org PDF) -- this link is DEAD: curl -sIL shows a 301 redirect from the exact PDF path straight to https://www.opec.org (homepage), which itself then 403s; url_verifier's OK was a false positive because 'Libya' trivially appears in the homepage's nav/metadata, not because the ASB PDF resolved. However, I found solid INDEPENDENT confirmation: a 2016 World Bank-commissioned consultancy report by Tractebel Engineering S.A. ('Libya - Supporting Electricity Sector Reform, Task B: Fuel Availability and Opportunities for Cost Reduction', hosted at documents1.worldbank.org) explicitly describes Libya's coastal gas transmission system as split into named segments, one of which is 'From Brega to Khoms (645 km) with a capacity of ~370 mmscf/d' -- this is an EXACT match to GEM's LengthKnown=645.00km, and it independently names this exact stretch as a real, distinct pipeline asset (also labelled 'El Khoms - El Brega Pipeline' in the report's utilization charts), not a GEM-derived or wiki-derived description. The same report states the coastal network's connection pipelines use 34-inch diameter -- consistent with GEM's Diameter=34.00in (a network-wide figure, not segment-specific, so treat as corroborating rather than dispositive). Status=operating is confirmed by the report's live 2017-2030 utilization/bottleneck forecasting for this exact segment (you don't forecast utilization of a pipe that doesn't exist and isn't flowing). Owner='Libyan National Oil Corp' is consistent with the report's description of NOC as the parent O&G authority and creator (2007) of General Gas Transmission and Distribution Company (GGT&D), the subsidiary that specifically builds/manages the natural gas distribution/transmission network -- GEM's NOC parent attribution is defensible, though GGT&D is the more precise operating subsidiary and isn't named in the GEM row. I verified the PDF is live (HTTP 200) via curl and pdftotext -layout locally, and confirmed 'Khoms', 'Brega', and '645' literally appear in the extracted text at the relevant passage; url_verifier's automated substring check FAILs on this URL only because it scans raw undecoded PDF bytes rather than extracted text (a known documented limitation for PDFs), not because the content is absent -- I manually verified the match per the tool's own guidance for this failure mode. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a transmission trunk segment (not a gathering/feeder line) per the same report's system-level treatment. DUPLICATE check against the 30-pipeline roster: no other PID shares this name, length (645km), or capacity (11.61 bcm/y) -- not a direct duplicate/relabel of a same-named entity.

This is decisive against a DUPLICATE flag: these are two real, separately-tracked physical lines per the primary source, not a GEM relabel/double-count of one pipe, so P6709 and P1859 should stay as separate rows. CLASSIFICATION holds (gas, transmission-grade feeder line into the Mellitah gas-gathering network, consistent with how the roster treats every other short Libyan inter-field segment). SPEC CONCERN: the OPEC table's capacity column header for this table is explicitly '(1,000 scm/yr)' (confirmed in the pdftotext output, e.g. Algeria section header on the same page layout) -- meaning the true capacity is 37,213 x 1,000 = 37,213,000 scm/yr = ~0.0372 bcm/yr. Sibling row P1859 converted this same table's units correctly (its OPEC figure of 3,879,921 -> GEM's recorded '3.88 bcm/y'), but P6709 instead recorded the bare OPEC digit as 'Capacity: 37213.00' with 'CapacityUnits: scm/yr' -- i.e. it dropped the x1,000 multiplier AND kept plain scm/yr instead of converting to bcm/y, so the recorded value reads as a physically implausible ~37,213 actual scm/yr (about 100 scm/day, far too small for an industrial gas line) when the real figure should read approximately 0.0372 bcm/yr. This is a genuine, source-confirmable spec/unit error, not a fabrication -- the underlying digits are an exact match to the primary source, only the scale/units are wrong. Caveat: I could not run these Wayback PDF URLs through url_verifier successfully -- the tool reports FAIL/'missing expected' for tokens like 'Bouri' and 'Bahr' against all three OPEC snapshots (both original opec.org, which now dead-redirect to the homepage, and the Wayback copies), because the verifier's plain-text substring check cannot read the compressed PDF byte stream; I confirmed the content manually via pdftotext -layout instead, which is the standard, more reliable extraction method for this class of document. resolutions.researcher_notes: Evidence supports a genuine double-count risk, though it does not resolve cleanly to 'yes, definitely redundant' vs 'no.' (1) P1862 Brega-Benghazi (396km) + P1863 Brega-Khoms (645km) + P1864 Khoms-Tripoli (201km) + this row P1865 Tripoli-Mellitah (158km) sum to exactly 1,400 km, retracing the identical Mellitah<->Benghazi coastal corridor that P0483 'Libya Coastal Gas Pipeline' also covers end-to-end as a single aggregate row (1,164 km). Both the 4-segment set and P0483 trace back to overlapping citations: the recovered OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 (which lists ONLY the 4 discrete Sirte-Oil-operated segments -- Brega/Benghazi, Brega/Khoms, Khoms/Tripoli, Tripoli/Mellitah -- with no aggregate 'Coastal Pipeline' total line of its own) and the World Bank/Tractebel 2017-18 report (which P0483's shard also used, and which this shard used independently). (2) The two source families do NOT even agree on how many physical trenches make up the western half: OPEC's table (and hence GEM's P1864/P1865 split) treats Khoms-Tripoli and Tripoli-Mellitah as two separate accounting segments (359 km combined), while the World Bank/Tractebel engineering report models the identical Mellitah<->Khoms run as ONE trench of only 222 km -- a 137 km (62%) gap that cannot be explained by rounding or unit error. This suggests OPEC's per-segment table may reflect tariff/ownership accounting boundaries (each stretch separately reported by Sirte Oil) rather than necessarily four separately-built physical pipelines, and raises the possibility the Tripoli split point is not a real physical joint recognized in independent engineering literature. (3) Separately, at least one LATER, smaller-spec 'Melitah-Tripoli'/'Tripoli-Mellitah' pipeline was built/completed circa 2005-2006 (ognnews.com project report; Al Wasat News 2006, Punj Lloyd contract, ~120 km, 200 MMcf/d, built to supply Zawiya power station) -- a different physical asset from the OPEC-table line this row's exact values (158km/34in/16.99 bcm/y) match, adding a further identification wrinkle but not itself evidence of double-counting against P0483. Net read: strong circumstantial evidence that P0483 (aggregate) and the P1862-P1865 segment set describe the SAME underlying physical corridor from overlapping sourcing, with an unreconciled ~20% total-length gap (1,400 km segment-sum vs 1,164 km aggregate) and an internally inconsistent western-half segmentation (OPEC's 2-segment Khoms-Tripoli/Tripoli-Mellitah split vs World Bank/Tractebel's single Mellitah-Khoms trench). This is a candidate for human review to decide whether P0483 should be retired/merged now that the more granular segment rows exist, or whether the segment set should itself be re-consolidated (e.g. merging P1864+P1865 into one Khoms-Mellitah row) to match the independent engineering source's trench boundaries -- not something this researcher can resolve unilaterally without fabricating a reconciliation.

(2) An independent 1970s-commissioning engineering incident-report paper (title: 'Explosion in the Gas Pipeline 36-inch diameter, Zelten-Brega', Hussein Albashik) describes a distinct '36in gas pipeline from Zelten to Brega' with its own rupture history (Aug 2014, Km 18) and 150 mmscfd design capacity from its 1970 commissioning — i.e. a real, physically documented gas asset independent of the 1961-built crude oil line (whose GEM wiki summary independently gives commissioning October 1961, separate from this line's 1970 commissioning) (this source itself is uncitable — academia.edu returned HTTP 403 to both WebFetch and url_verifier — so treat this only as directional evidence, not a stageable ref). (3) A WebSearch synthesis (source unconfirmed) also describes 'a 30-inch gas pipeline' linking Zelten field to the Brega LNG/petrochemical complex, suggesting there may even be more than one gas-carrying line/lateral in this corridor, further supporting that the gas and oil assets are not simply the same line re-entered. If the two lines are truly parallel and co-built/co-routed (which fits '36in, Sirte Oil, same corridor' appearing twice in OPEC's own 2012 tables), a shared/near-identical length would be expected and is not itself evidence of duplication — but it does mean GEM's currently entered 277 km for P1866 cannot be independently justified as reflecting a materially longer or different route than P0599's 171.62 km, and the discrepancy should be resolved (most likely by correcting P1866's length toward ~172 km) independently of the redundancy question. Net read: keep both P0599 (oil) and P1866 (gas) as distinct entities — the weight of evidence favors two real, separate, same-corridor pipelines — but recommend a length correction on P1866, not a merge/removal of either row.

resolutions.researcher_notes: P3988 (Fargh–Sarir, this row) and P1861 (Farigh-Intesar, per this batch's own P1861 shard) are NOT duplicates of each other: P1861 traces to OPEC ASB2012 Table 4.10 data from 2011 (110 mi / 177 km, 24 in diameter, 7.08 bcm/y capacity -- an older, pre-existing Waha line running Fargh field to the Intisar field/103 complex), while P3988 traces to a 2020 Waha Oil Company announcement of a NEWLY commissioned 97 km line running Fargh field to Sarir GAS/POWER STATION -- different destination, different specs, different vintage, and my primary Waha-2020 source itself distinguishes the two: it describes the Fargh-Sarir line (this row) separately from ongoing supply 'to the Intisar A field ... 70 million cubic meters of gas' (the P1861 corridor), i.e. Fargh field feeds two distinct downstream lines. Good evidence these are two real, separate pieces of infrastructure. P3987 (Intisar–Sarir) is a different question: per GEM's own wiki text, P3987 is described as running from Intisar oil field (Sirte Basin) to Sarir oil field (Cyrenaica), status is explicitly '(presumed operating)' based solely on a 2017 agreement with 'no direct evidence' (GEM's own wording), sourced to a single eanlibya.com URL I could not locate/verify (search engines returned no matching eanlibya.com page under that slug) plus a generic Waha Facebook page and a wahaoil.ly article titled 'إستئناف تغذية خط محطة السرير بشكل اعتيادي' ('resumption of normal supply to the Sarir station LINE') -- that title describes a SUPPLY LINE TO SARIR STATION resuming normal operation, which is the same phrasing/subject as the Fargh–Sarir gas-to-power-station story I independently corroborated for P3988 (Libya Observer 2022-07-24: 'Fargh field ... restarted pumping gas to the Sarir power station'; multiple Arabic sources found this session state plainly 'حقل الفارغ يمثل المصدر الرئيس لتغذية محطة السرير' -- 'the Fargh field is THE MAIN source supplying Sarir station'). I found no independent corroboration anywhere (English or Arabic press, 2017-2026) of a physically distinct 'Intisar oil field to Sarir oil field' gas pipeline separate from the Fargh-to-Sarir line. My working suspicion (not confirmed) is that P3987 may be describing the same underlying Fargh→Sarir gas supply chain/network under an older, less-precise 2017-vintage name (with Intisar possibly an intermediate junction or a source-confusion with the separate Fargh-Intisar line, P1861) rather than a third, independently-built pipeline -- but I could not verify this either way from primary sources, so flagging as UNRESOLVED per protocol rather than asserting duplication. Recommend a human reviewer compare P3987's actual GEM sourcing (the eanlibya.com/wahaoil.ly citations) against this shard's Fargh-Sarir sourcing before any merge/delete decision.

resolutions.researcher_notes: STRONG, CORROBORATED FINDING: P6705 (16in) is misclassified -- the 16in Wafa-Mellitah line is the OIL/CONDENSATE line, not a gas line, and does not belong in the gas tracker. Every source found that distinguishes the two parallel Wafa-Mellitah lines by diameter+service agrees, with no exceptions: (1) Offshore Technology's 'Wafa-Mellitah Gas' market-data page: 32in max diameter, carries natural gas / 'on-specification gas', ~13 MMSm3/day. (2) Offshore Technology's separate 'Wafa-Mellitah Oil' market-data page: 16in max diameter, product type 'Crude oil' (condensate). (3) Mellitah Oil & Gas Company Achievements page (operator's own site): 'The 525 Km onshore pipeline system comprises of 32" gas and 16" oil/condensates pipelines. Both pipelines run in parallel from Wafa Desert Plant to Mellitah... the sale gas is exported to Italy and the oil/condensate, after further treatment for LPG fractionation, is exported.' (4) Mellitah Oil & Gas gas-division production page: '32 inches... Carries: On-specification sales gas... ~13 MMSm3/day' vs '16 inches... Carries: Oil and condensate mixture... ~23,000 bbl/d NGL and ~38,000 bbl/d oil/condensate.' (5) Mellitah Oil & Gas Wafa-field site page: the field has a separate 'Gas compression station to Mellitah' and 'Oil pumping station to Mellitah' -- two distinct facilities/lines at the source. (6) Mellitah Oil & Gas Mellitah-Complex page: the Wafa Coastal Plant (within Mellitah Complex) specifically processes 'oil and natural gas liquids from the Wafa field', separately from the Mellitah Plant which handles gas/condensate from the offshore Sabratha platform (Bahr Essalam field) -- i.e. the Wafa-sourced onshore stream landing via the 16in line is treated as an oil/NGL stream, not sales gas. No source anywhere describes a 16in GAS line on this corridor, or a 32in oil/condensate line. CONCLUSION: P6705 (16in, currently in GGIT/gas tracker as 'Wafa-Mellitah Gas Pipeline') and P0484 (32in) are NOT duplicate/redundant entries of the same pipeline -- they are two real, physically distinct, genuinely parallel pipelines, correctly kept as separate rows. But P6705 is in the WRONG TRACKER: by diameter and service it is the oil/condensate line and belongs in GOIT (oil tracker), not GGIT. ACTION FLAG: gem.wiki already has a page titled 'Wafa-Mellitah_Oil_Pipeline' (surfaced incidentally in web search results during this research), which suggests GEM/GOIT may already carry this pipeline as a separate oil-tracker entry under that name -- before reclassifying/moving P6705, check GOIT for an existing 'Wafa-Mellitah Oil Pipeline' row to avoid creating a duplicate; if one already exists, P6705's gas-tracker row is likely a redundant/erroneous entry that should be removed (or corrected in place) rather than moved.

resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT a duplicate — sources indicate GEM's P6709 and P1859 represent two genuinely different, parallel physical pipelines on the same Bouri-to-Bahr Essalam/Sabratah corridor, not a double-count of one line. Evidence: OPEC's Annual Statistical Bulletin tabulates this field-pair as TWO adjacent-but-separate rows in every edition checked (ASB2012, ASB2013, ASB2017): a 10-inch line carrying dehydrated GAS and a 4-inch line carrying CONDENSATE. ASB2017 Table 9.9 makes the pairing explicit: 'Bouri offshore/Bahr Es Salam (2) | Mellitha Oil & Gas | 2 x 12 [mi] | 4, 10 [in]' — the '(2)' notation plus '2 x 12' means two parallel 12-mile lines, one 4in and one 10in. Independently, Mellitah Oil & Gas's own 2019 prequalification tender for the 'Bouri Gas Upgrading Project' (BGUP) describes new '10" CS and 4" CS pipelines 20 km long connecting DP4 to Sabratah Platform for dehydrated gas and condensate export' — the same twin-diameter, same-route configuration (gas line + separate condensate line). So P6709 (4in) = the condensate line, P1859 (10in) = the gas line of the same corridor: different specs because they are different pipes, not a GEM data error in that specific sense. Two open caveats worth flagging to the researcher, though: (1) P1859's GEM length (32 km) doesn't match the ~12-12.4 mi (~19-20 km) that ASB2013/ASB2017 converge on for BOTH lines — 32km (=20mi) traces to the earlier ASB2012 edition's figure for that same row, which later ASB editions revised down; P1859's length may merit a separate correction check. (2) The mellitahog.ly 2019 document frames its 10in/4in pipes as NEW/planned BGUP construction (feasibility stage 2019; Saipem's ~$1bn contract 2023; first gas still targeted Sept 2026 per Libya Herald), while the OPEC ASB entries (2011-2013 data) already show a same-diameter pairing years earlier — implying an older, smaller Bouri-Sabratha tie-in predates BGUP and BGUP is now building new/expanded twin lines of the same diameters on the same route. Current-day operating status of GEM's specific P6709/P1859 assets vs. the incoming BGUP lines is not resolved by the sources found; recommend a follow-up check once BGUP reaches first gas (targeted Sept 2026) to confirm whether these rows should be updated to as-built BGUP specs or retired/merged.

resolutions.researcher_notes: P6713 and P1855 are NOT simple duplicates of each other, but P6713 IS a genuine misclassification. Multiple independent sources agree the Bahr Essalam (Sabratha platform) field is tied to Mellitah by exactly TWO separate subsea lines, not one: a 36-in line carrying GAS and a 10-in line carrying CONDENSATE (liquids). Offshore Technology: '10-in diameter pipeline through which condensate is directly pumped and conveyed to Mellitah'; Offshore Magazine: '36-in. and 10-in. pipelines taking gas and condensate from the platform 100-km south to Mellitah.' P6713 has diameter=10in — it IS the condensate line, not a second gas line, despite carrying the same 'Gas Pipeline' name as P1855 (diameter=36in, the true gas line). The likely mechanical origin of the GEM duplication: OPEC's own ASB tables list BOTH diameters under one shared row/label ('Bahr Assalam/Mellitah ... 68.2 mi ... 36 in ... 9,199,943' and a second row 'Bahr Assalam/Mellitah ... 68.2 mi ... 10 in ... 465,166', both under the 'Gas pipelines' table heading even though the 10-in line is physically condensate) — someone appears to have carried both OPEC rows into GGIT as two separate 'Gas Pipeline' entities instead of recognizing the second as condensate. Critically, GEM ALREADY tracks this exact 10-in condensate line correctly, under GOIT (oil/NGL tracker): P6457 'Sabratha-Mellitah Condensate Pipeline' — Start='Sabratha platform', End='Mellitah', Length=107 km, Diameter=10 in, Status=operating — near-identical specs to P6713 (Bahr Assalam/Mellitah, 109 km, 10 in, operating). FINDING: P6713 in GGIT (gas) is a duplicate/misclassified twin of P6457 in GOIT (oil/NGL); it belongs in the oil tracker, not the gas tracker, and once reclassified is redundant with the already-existing P6457. Recommend retiring/removing P6713 from GGIT (or merging its provenance into P6457) rather than treating it as a distinct gas pipeline needing its own refs going forward.

resolutions.researcher_notes: NOT a double-count — evidence points to two real, parallel gas pipelines, not one line entered twice. Internal comparison: P1858 (34in, capacity 4,134,806) and P6714 (10in, capacity 258,425) share the identical length (131.96 km) and identical start/end (Bu-Attifel Oil Field -> Intesar Oil field, Sirte Basin). OPEC ASB2013 Table 4.10 ('Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2012', p.~74-75, recovered via Wayback, pdftotext-confirmed) lists them as TWO SEPARATE table rows with different operators: 'Bu-Attifel/Intesar   Mellitah Oil and Gas   82.46mi   34in   4,134,806' and 'Bu-Attifel/Intesar (103A)   Eni Oil   82.46mi   10in   258,425' -- exact match to P1858 and P6714 respectively, down to the capacity figures. OPEC ASB2017 Table 9.9 (2016 data, recovered via Wayback) independently corroborates this across a later edition, listing the connection as 'Bu Attifel/Intisar (2)' -- explicitly '(2)' = two lines -- '2 x 82mi', diameters '34, 10', joint owner field 'Mellitah Oil & Gas, Eni Oil' (i.e. one line per operator). Two OPEC editions four years apart, independently compiled, agree that this is a twinned/parallel pipeline pair (same corridor, different operators/diameters/capacities), not a single pipeline double-entered. Recommend: NOT a candidate for merging/removal; if anything, GEM's Owner/Operator data for these two rows should be checked to confirm P1858=Mellitah Oil & Gas and P6714=Eni Oil, matching the OPEC operator split (out of scope for this ref-only shard).
